mainEntity.name: I have been arrested for assault but not charged — should I call now?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The strongest moment to act is before charge. Decisions taken at the police station shape the rest of the case.

mainEntity.name: Will I get bail after an assault charge?

acceptedAnswer.text: Bail turns on the allegation, prior history, and the conditions that can realistically be offered. The first call covers what is and is not likely.

mainEntity.name: The complainant is a family member — does that change how the case is handled?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Domestic-related allegations attract specific procedures around protective measures, disclosure, and witness handling. These are addressed at the first conference.

mainEntity.name: I was acting in self-defence — does that matter?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Self-defence is a complete defence to most assault charges in England and Wales. It applies where the force used was honestly believed to be necessary and was reasonable in the circumstances as the person believed them to be. Whether self-defence runs in a given case turns on the evidence, witness accounts, forensic findings, and the defendant's own account.
